Implement integrity controls and checksums

threats.attackDescription: Debugger claims it never sent the command or data that Sensor Diagnostic Controller received and acted upon
threats.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from Debugger are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender

threats.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on embedded bus DF-8 between Debugger and Sensor Diagnostic Controller
threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a logic analyzer to the embedded bus and captures all traffic
threats.causeDescription: Embedded bus communication is unencrypted and physically accessible — data can be passively captured

threats.threatDescription: Request flooding: Attacker overwhelms Sensor Diagnostic Controller with excessive incoming requests
threats.attackDescription: Attacker sends a high volume of requests via the data flow, exhausting the processing capacity of Sensor Diagnostic Controller
threats.causeDescription: No rate limiting or request throttling protecting Sensor Diagnostic Controller from high-volume input via Debugger

threats.threatDescription: Privilege escalation via DF-8 debug interface on Sensor Diagnostic Controller
threats.attackDescription: Attacker uses the DF-8 interface to halt the processor, reads security keys and modifies execution flow to bypass access controls
threats.causeDescription: JTAG or SWD interface provides full processor access — attacker can halt CPU and modify execution flow

threats.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface
threats.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
threats.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification

threats.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface
threats.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
threats.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection

threats.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed
threats.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
threats.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown

threats.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface
threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
threats.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment

threats.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable
threats.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
threats.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack

threats.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware
threats.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
threats.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification

threats.attackDescription: Attacker opens the enclosure without triggering any alarm, gaining access to internal components
threats.causeDescription: No tamper detection mechanism — unauthorized opening is undetected

threats.threatDescription: Side-channel observation — sensitive data extracted via physical measurements
threats.attackDescription: Attacker measures power consumption or EM emissions and extracts cryptographic keys
threats.causeDescription: Physical boundary provides no electromagnetic shielding — internal operations are observable

threats.threatDescription: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack
threats.attackDescription: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability
threats.causeDescription: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed

threats.threatDescription: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach
threats.attackDescription: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication
threats.causeDescription: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed

assumptions.text: The detector is mounted so that its debug connector cannot be reached without opening the housing; only service staff of the integrator open it.
The controller the detector is built into authenticates itself on the sensor link and keeps the link token secret.
